hexanal.uncertainty_basis: Table 4 prints '324 +/- 34.3' ug kg-1 for roasted peas; footnote f: 'The concentrations are the means of three repeated measurements +/- standard deviation (to three significant figures).' 34.3/324 = 10.59%.
hexanal.value_provenance_note: 2026-08-28 (Wave W): CORRECTED FROM THE PRIMARY SOURCE. The paper's Table 4 prints this concentration directly as '324 +/- 34.3' ug kg-1 for roasted peas, and prints OAV 72 in a separate column derived FROM it. See wave_w_primary_source_correction below for the full quote and for why the exact divisibility by 4.5 that Wave I flagged is explained rather than coincidental. THE PRIOR NOTE IS RETAINED VERBATIM BELOW because it is the audit record. ||| PRIOR NOTE (Wave I, superseded): 2026-08-27 (Wave I, cold-start red-team finding): this value is NOT an independently measured concentration in this repo's chain of custody. The arithmetic is exact: OAV 72 (the value the intake registry records for this anchor, the roasted-pea carryover point, 324 ug/kg) x 4.5 ppb, where 4.5 ppb is THIS REPO'S OWN hexanal odour-detection threshold -- itself a compilation-level number that has never been read off a primary table (see the hexanal ODT anchor's harmonization_note in this file; published aqueous hexanal ODTs span 0.3-14 ug/L). 72 x 4.5 = 324.0 to the digit. It is therefore possible that the source reports 324 ug/kg directly and the OAV is the derived quantity -- but that has NOT been confirmed against the paper, and the exact divisibility by our own unsourced constant is precisely why the two readings cannot be told apart from inside the repo. Scored as a hold-out point it is a consistency check against our own threshold, not an external measurement, and it MOVES if that threshold is ever corrected.

wave_w_primary_source_correction.access: Full text obtained by the repository owner via interlibrary loan, 2026-08-28, read directly from data/articles/bi2020.pdf (gitignored; the PDF is not committed). Identity confirmed from the PDF first page: 'Characterization of Key Aroma Compounds in Raw and Roasted Peas (Pisum sativum L.) by Application of Instrumental and Sensory Techniques', Shuang Bi, Xinxing Xu, Dongsheng Luo, Fei Lao, Xueli Pang, Qun Shen, Xiaosong Hu, Jihong Wu, 'Cite This: J. Agric. Food Chem. 2020, 68, 2718-2727'.
wave_w_primary_source_correction.quantification_class: External calibration curve against an internal standard (2,4,6-trimethylpyridine), R2 = 0.997, triplicate, SPME-GC-MS. NOT stable-isotope dilution -- no deuterated hexanal was used -- so this is weaker than the Hofmann and Yiltirak sulfur anchors and is labelled as such rather than levelled up.
wave_w_primary_source_correction.quoted_table: Table 4, 'Concentrations and OAVs of the odorants in raw and roasted peas'. The hexanal row, transcribed verbatim across its printed columns (no., compound, odor threshold, selected ions, calibration equation, R2, concentration in raw peas, concentration in roasted peas, OAV raw, OAV roasted): '3  hexanal  4.5k  56, 44  y = 0.003300x + 1.051800  0.997  1260 +/- 114a  324 +/- 34.3b  280  72'. Table footnotes, verbatim: 'cOdor threshold (OT) (ug kg-1) in water obtained from the literature.' ; 'eVariables: x is the peak area relative to that of the internal standard, 2,4,6-trimethylpyridine, and y is the concentration (ug ...) relative to that of the internal standard, 2,4,6-trimethylpyridine.' ; 'fThe concentrations are the means of three repeated measurements +/- standard deviation (to three significant figures).' ; 'gMean values in the same row with different letters are significantly different at a level of [p < 0.05].' ; 'h[OAV is the] ratio of concentration to odor threshold.' ; 'kOdor threshold obtained from [van] Gemert.41' The body text independently reproduces both figures: '3-methylbutanoic acid (4580 ug kg-1) had the highest concentration in raw peas, followed by hexanal (1260 ug kg-1)' and 'followed by hexanal (324 ug kg-1; OAV = 72)'.
wave_w_primary_source_correction.the_coincidence_is_explained_and_it_vind: Wave I flagged that 1260 was EXACTLY divisible by this repository's own unsourced hexanal odour-detection threshold of 4.5 ppb, and treated that exact divisibility as the tell that the two readings could not be told apart from inside the repo. The paper resolves it: Bi et al.'s own odour threshold column prints '4.5' ug kg-1 for hexanal, attributed by footnote k to van Gemert (ref 41). The repository's 4.5 ppb and the paper's 4.5 ug kg-1 are the SAME literature threshold, which is why the division came out exact. Side effect worth recording: the repo's hexanal ODT of 4.5 ppb, previously a compilation-level number with no primary table behind it, now has an independent published source agreeing with it to the digit -- though it is the same underlying van Gemert compilation, so this is CORROBORATION OF THE VALUE'S PROVENANCE, NOT AN INDEPENDENT MEASUREMENT OF THE THRESHOLD.
wave_w_primary_source_correction.the_number_does_not_move: OLD 1260.0 ppb -> NEW 1260.0 ppb. FOLD CHANGE 1.000x. This is a PROVENANCE correction and an UNCERTAINTY addition, not a value correction, and it is reported that way rather than dressed up as a fix. What changes is what the number is entitled to be called: it was 'a consistency check against our own threshold'; it is now an external measurement with a stated replicate spread.
wave_w_primary_source_correction.verdict: THE WAVE I RED-TEAM POSED A TWO-BRANCH QUESTION AND THE PAPER ANSWERS IT: the concentration is the MEASURED quantity and the OAV is the DERIVED one, not the other way round. Table 4's footnote h defines the OAV as the 'ratio of concentration to odor threshold', and the concentration column carries a standard deviation (1260 +/- 114) while the OAV column carries none. So the repository's arithmetic (OAV 280 x 4.5 ppb = 1260) was running the paper's own calculation BACKWARDS and landing on the right number by construction.
